root_cause.text: The sysfs mode enablement in tmc-etr is split into two separate critical regions (buffer allocation and hardware enable) without holding the lock across both, allowing a concurrent perf mode enablement to set drvdata->etr_buf in between, causing a spurious WARN_ON and inconsistent state.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and patch diff show the race scenario explicitly: sysfs allocates buffer in one critical section, then perf gets in and enables hardware (setting drvdata->etr_buf) before sysfs' second critical section tries to enable hardware and triggers WARN_ON(drvdata->etr_buf). The fix adds a re-check for CS_MODE_PERF after re-acquiring the spinlock in tmc_enable_etr_sink_sysfs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid race condition between sysfs and perf mode by checking if sink is in perf mode before enabling sysfs, returning -EBUSY and freeing allocated buffer.
intent_record.what: Added a check after acquiring the spinlock in tmc_enable_etr_sink_sysfs to detect if the sink is already in CS_MODE_PERF; if so, the sysfs buffer is freed and -EBUSY is returned.
intent_record.how: Prevents the sysfs enable path from proceeding when the sink is already claimed by perf mode, avoiding a race condition that could corrupt state.
